discovery: Development of next-generation DNA sequencing (sequencing by synthesis with reversible-terminator chemistry)
rationale: Recent Chemistry prizes went to MOFs (2025), protein design and structure prediction (2024), and quantum dots (2023), so the committee has been rotating across subfields. A chemistry-driven tool for the life sciences is a likely next pick. Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis rests on fluorescent reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry, and it made genomics vastly cheaper and faster. It has already won the Breakthrough Prize (2022) and the Millennium Technology Prize (2020), and it shows up often on Nobel shortlists.
